For Copycat-style analogy, the groupoid calculus supplies an exact baseline. Correspondences can be reversed, chained, and reframed while invariant observations remain stable. It does not yet model salience, competition, probabilistic confidence, or contextual slippage. Those mechanisms concern selection among correspondences; the present theorems concern conclusions guaranteed once an exact correspondence is fixed.

Isomorphism is always relative to a signature. Objects may be isomorphic with respect to adjacency and nonisomorphic after colors, weights, time, or interpretations are added. The positive and negative theorems are therefore complementary. Structural invariance covers every internal observation; semantic collision varies an external coordinate.

\section{Future research}
Finite characteristic formulas may determine when an observational language classifies pointed models up to isomorphism and how modal depth measures identification cost. Graded modalities are natural candidates.

Networks of analogies raise a coherence question. Transport around cycles may produce holonomy; globally consistent meaning assignments should correspond to trivial holonomy, perhaps testable on a cycle basis.

Approximate analogies in probabilistic transition systems should replace equality by error bounds. Modal depth is expected to control error accumulation because nested boxes repeatedly expose transition defects.

The collision theorem also suggests an orbit criterion. Any interpretation recoverable from invariant truth must be constant on automorphism orbits. For finite models, counting modalities may make orbit constancy sufficient for definability.

Finally, bisimulation should be compared with isomorphism as a measure of semantic resolution. Modal logic often sees exactly bisimulation-invariant distinctions while ignoring identity and cardinal information. Matching languages to their natural equivalences would extend the present boundary analysis.

\section{Conclusion}
A reversible renaming of worlds and atoms preserving transitions and valuations preserves every modal truth. The result extends to global validity, chains of analogies, and conjugated correspondences. Exact analogies therefore possess coherent groupoid structure.

External interpretation can nevertheless vary while all those observations remain fixed. The singleton collision isolates the boundary: truth preservation is indexed by an observational language. Within that language, isomorphism is decisive; beyond it, semantic claims require additional structure, vocabulary, or grounding.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence, Tuple

    ATOM = "atom"
    BOTTOM = "bottom"
    IMP = "imp"
    BOX = "box"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Formula:
    kind: Kind
    atom: str | None = None
    left: "Formula | None" = None
    right: "Formula | None" = None

    @staticmethod
    def var(name: str) -> "Formula":
        return Formula(Kind.ATOM, atom=name)

    @staticmethod
    def bottom() -> "Formula":
        return Formula(Kind.BOTTOM)

    def implies(self, other: "Formula") -> "Formula":
        return Formula(Kind.IMP, left=self, right=other)

    def box(self) -> "Formula":
        return Formula(Kind.BOX, left=self)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.kind is Kind.ATOM:
            return str(self.atom)
        if self.kind is Kind.BOTTOM:
            return "⊥"
        if self.kind is Kind.BOX:
            return f"□({self.left})"
        return f"({self.left} → {self.right})"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Model:
    worlds: Tuple[str, ...]
    atoms: Tuple[str, ...]
    edges: frozenset[Tuple[str, str]]
    true_at: frozenset[Tuple[str, str]]

    def successors(self, world: str) -> Iterable[str]:
        return (target for source, target in self.edges if source == world)


def satisfies(model: Model, world: str, formula: Formula) -> bool:
    """Evaluate a modal formula at one world."""
    if formula.kind is Kind.ATOM:
        assert formula.atom is not None
        return (world, formula.atom) in model.true_at
    if formula.kind is Kind.BOTTOM:
        return False
    if formula.kind is Kind.IMP:
        assert formula.left is not None and formula.right is not None
        return (not satisfies(model, world, formula.left)) or satisfies(
            model, world, formula.right
        )
    assert formula.left is not None
    return all(satisfies(model, nxt, formula.left) for nxt in model.successors(world))


def rename_formula(formula: Formula, atom_map: Mapping[str, str]) -> Formula:
    """Transport all atomic names through a bijection."""
    if formula.kind is Kind.ATOM:
        assert formula.atom is not None
        return Formula.var(atom_map[formula.atom])
    if formula.kind is Kind.BOTTOM:
        return formula
    if formula.kind is Kind.BOX:
        assert formula.left is not None
        return rename_formula(formula.left, atom_map).box()
    assert formula.left is not None and formula.right is not None
    return rename_formula(formula.left, atom_map).implies(
        rename_formula(formula.right, atom_map)
    )


def check_isomorphism(
    source: Model,
    target: Model,
    world_map: Mapping[str, str],
    atom_map: Mapping[str, str],

    """Check bijectivity plus preservation and reflection of all model data."""
    if set(world_map) != set(source.worlds) or set(world_map.values()) != set(target.worlds):

    current = tuple(Formula.var(a) for a in atoms) + (Formula.bottom(),)
    all_forms = list(current)
    for _ in range(depth):
        previous = tuple(all_forms)
        new_forms = [p.box() for p in previous]

        frozenset({("start", "ok"), ("safe", "ok"), ("risk", "alarm")}),

    atom_map = {"ok": "green", "alarm": "red"}

        ("green", "red"),

        frozenset((world_map[w], atom_map[a]) for w, a in source.true_at),

    tests = formulas(source.atoms, 1)
    assert check_isomorphism(source, target, world_map, atom_map)

    )
    total = len(source.worlds) * len(tests)
    print(f"Structural invariance: {agreements}/{total} transported evaluations agree.")
    assert agreements == total

    """Show that two renamings and their composite carry identical truth values."""
    p = Formula.var("ready")
    safety = p.box().implies(p)
    first = {"ready": "enabled"}
    second = {"enabled": "active"}
    composite = {key: second[value] for key, value in first.items()}
    sequential = rename_formula(rename_formula(safety, first), second)
    direct = rename_formula(safety, composite)
    print(f"Composition: sequential formula {sequential}; direct formula {direct}.")
    assert sequential == direct

    singleton = Model(
        ("only",),
        ("observed",),
        frozenset({("only", "only")}),
        frozenset({("only", "observed")}),

    )

        f"but labels are {external_meaning_a} and {external_meaning_b}."
    )
    assert agreements == len(tests)
    assert external_meaning_a != external_meaning_b


def main() -> None:
    demo_structural_invariance()
    demo_composition()
    demo_meaning_collision()
